REX ONE: Rapid Extraction Multi-Purpose Rescue Stretcher
Product URL: https://www.anchortex.com/products/rapid-extraction-rex-one-multi-purpose-extraction-stretcher
Manufacturer page: https://rapidextraction.com/rex-systems/rex-one/
Spec sheet: REX overview brochure
Keywords (Ricky's sheet): Primary: rescue stretcher (200/mo, KD0). Secondary: stair stretcher (80, KD0), confined space rescue stretcher (10), evacuation stretcher (10). Ricky's note: rescue stretcher is the best term for the REX pages; check that stair stretcher fits the product before using it.
Recommended H1 and Subtitle
H1: Rapid Extraction Multi-Purpose Rescue Stretcher with All-Terrain Wheels – REX ONE
Current H1: REX ONE – Multi-Purpose Extraction Stretcher
Subtitle: Tri-Fold Mobile Evacuation Stretcher, Backboard, and Treatment Cot That Lets One Responder Move a Patient Over Almost Any Terrain
Current subtitle: Rapid Extraction RexONE Patient Evacuation Stretcher
Revised Product Description
Headings marked [H2] should be set as H2 on the page.
The Rapid Extraction REX ONE is a multi-purpose rescue stretcher that lets a single responder move a patient quickly and safely over almost any terrain. The tri-fold mobile stretcher converts into a backboard or a patient treatment cot, so one device covers extraction, transport, and treatment for EMS, fire, law enforcement, and event medical teams.
Centered, balanced wheels and a telescoping pull handle give the REX ONE 360° maneuverability, and its 20” puncture-proof all-terrain tires need no maintenance. The evacuation stretcher is ready to roll in under 30 seconds and folds into a backpack carrying case, which makes it a good fit for mass casualty incidents, medical surge, HazMat operations, and active shooter response.
Frame: Rugged T-6 aerospace aluminum with a patented tri-fold panel system (head, center, and foot panels)
Configurations: Converts to a backboard, mobile stretcher, or patient treatment cot, and adjusts for supine and Fowler’s positions
Setup: Ready to roll in under 30 seconds
Load Capacity: 400 lbs
Ground Clearance: 10” from the ground to the base
Folded Size: 25”×18”
Wheels: Quick-release, interchangeable wheel system with 20” puncture-proof, airless all-terrain tires that resist heat and cold
Pull Handle: Telescoping pull handle that folds under the foot panel
Kickstands: Head and foot kickstands extend to turn the stretcher into a treatment cot
Headrest: Adjustable locking headrest
Patient Straps: Interchangeable patient restraint straps (set of 3)
Fenders: Protective wheel fenders keep the patient clear of the tires, with color-coded tabs for quick assembly
Cleaning: Fully decontaminable
Includes: Backpack carrying case
Colors: Blue, Red, Yellow, or Black
Warranty: 1-year warranty
Country of Manufacture: Made in the U.S.A.
Available Models and Options
REX ONE – Standard Tires: 20” all-terrain tires for most conditions; Blue, Red, Yellow, or Black
REX ONE – Sand Tires: Sand tires for beaches and sandy ground; Blue, Red, Yellow, or Black
Accessories: Bike tow attachment (tow bar and hitch) and removable IV pole
[H2] Uses
The REX ONE suits any team that needs to move patients with fewer responders, from everyday calls to large incidents.
Typical uses include:
EMS and fire departments: Move patients over rough ground, grass, gravel, and long distances to the ambulance
Mass casualty incidents and medical surge: One responder per patient frees others for patient care
Law enforcement and SWAT: Rapid patient extraction during active shooter and tactical operations
HazMat operations: The fully decontaminable stretcher can be cleaned after use
Events, venues, campuses, and beaches: Patient transport across large sites, with sand tires for the beach
Bike patrols: With the bike tow attachment, a bike team can tow the stretcher to the patient
Explore Anchortex's Evacuation Chairs and Stretchers collection for more evacuation equipment.
[H2] Frequently Asked Questions
Can one person use the REX ONE?
Yes. The REX ONE is designed for rapid deployment by a single responder, and the balanced wheels and telescoping pull handle let one person move the patient.
Can the REX ONE go down the stairs?
For stairs and steep ground, choose the REX DCS. It is the REX ONE with a Descent Control System hand brake for controlled descent down stairwells and steep terrain.
What is the difference between standard and sand tires?
The standard 20” all-terrain tires are puncture-proof and handle most conditions. Sand tires are designed for beaches and sandy ground.
How is the REX ONE stored?
The rescue stretcher folds in three to 25”×18” and packs into its backpack carrying case, so it stows in a vehicle or closet and deploys quickly.
[H2] About Rapid Extraction REX Stretchers
REX stretchers fold in three for compact storage and roll on airless all-terrain wheels, so one responder can move a patient over stairs, rough ground, and long distances.
The REX line includes:
REX ONE: Multi-purpose extraction stretcher that converts to a backboard, mobile stretcher, or treatment cot
REX DCS: The REX ONE with a Descent Control System hand brake for stairs and steep ground
REX DCS/CF: The REX DCS for correctional facilities, with Humane Restraint cuffs and full body restraint straps
[H2] About Rapid Extraction
Rapid Extraction (REX EMS, LLC) of Glendora, California, designs and builds REX stretchers in the U.S.A., and REX stretchers won an EMS World Innovation Award.
Meta Title and Description
Meta title (54 characters): Rapid Extraction REX ONE Rescue Stretcher at Anchortex
Current meta title: REX ONE – Multi-Purpose Extraction Stretcher | Anchortex
Meta description (154 characters): Shop the Rapid Extraction REX ONE rescue stretcher, a tri-fold mobile stretcher, backboard, and treatment cot that lets one responder move a patient fast.
Current meta description (240 characters): Rapid Extraction REX extraction stretchers are a multi-functional, collapsible, all terrain stretcher designed to move the injured over varied terrain and conditions, faster and easier than ever before. Government and GSA pricing available.
Notes and Questions
Keywords: Ricky's primary keyword "rescue stretcher" is in the H1, the first sentence, a FAQ, the meta title, and the meta description. The search results for it are rescue stretcher product pages (basket, scoop, SKED, and roll-up stretchers from Ferno, CMC, and Spencer), so a wheeled rescue stretcher fits. "Evacuation stretcher" is in the subtitle and intro.
Stair stretcher: Ricky asked to check this one. The results are stair chairs and stretchers that carry patients down the stairs (Stryker Stair-PRO, Ferno), plus a carpet stretching tool. Rapid Extraction says stair use is for the REX DCS, which has the descent control brake, not the REX ONE. So I did not use "stair stretcher" here; I suggest it for the REX DCS page. The FAQ "Can the REX ONE go down the stairs?" sends stair buyers to the REX DCS.
"Confined space rescue stretcher": the results are SKED and roll-up stretchers that can be lowered through tight spaces. The REX ONE is a wheeled stretcher, so I did not use it.
WEIGHT: the Rapid Extraction web page, the Life-Assist spec sheet, Bound Tree, and our page say 42 lbs, but the REX overview brochure says "approx. 48 lbs." I left the weight out until you confirm. I suggest 42 lbs (48 lbs is the REX DCS/CF weight).
OPEN SIZE: our page, the Rapid Extraction web page, and Bound Tree say 75”×18” fully assembled; the brochure says 75”×26” deployed and the Life-Assist sheet says 75”×25”. 18” is the folded width, so the open width with wheels is probably 26”. I left the open size out; the folded size (25”×18”) agrees in all sources.
Duplicate content: our current description is the Rapid Extraction website text word for word (Bound Tree uses the same bullets). The new copy is fully rewritten.
Accessories: our page lists Bike Tow Kit, Bike Hitch, and IV Pole as options, but they are not variants. Do we sell them? The spec sheet also lists snow/ice tires and strap extenders, which I left out.
Sand tires: the sand tire variants are $4,020, $855 more than standard ($3,165). No compare-at price on any variant. Bound Tree lists the REX ONE at $4,346.99. No change made.
Shipping weight: all 8 variants are set to 75 lbs. Is that the boxed weight with the carrying case?
Collections: the REX ONE is only in the Evacuation Chairs and Stretchers collection. Most buyers are EMS, fire, and police teams. Should it also go in Public Safety Gear?
Current meta description says "Government and GSA pricing available." Is that still true?
Left out: "does the work of 4 to 6 responders," "Golden Hour solution," and "the only patient transport product" claims, custom colors, the 180° turn radius from the brochure (the web page says 360° maneuverability, which I used), and the patent number.
Images: the page has only one image (blue). Would you like me to add Rapid Extraction photos (treatment cot, backboard, folded in the backpack, other colors)? The current image alt text is the old product title.
